entries.not_relevant_because: The family's one manuscript, 'An asymptotic formula for the number of totients', counts distinct totient values V(x) and proves V(x) ~ (x/log x)·G_m·A(1;θ) and V(cx)/V(x) → c. It never asserts that some value has exactly one preimage under φ, nor that every value has at least two. Its nearest fibre statements do not decide the question: (i) the introduction cites OpenAITotientFibers2026, Theorem 1.1, for infinitely many v with more than v^(1-ε) preimages, describing it as concerning large individual fibres and as not an input to the proof; (ii) companion.tex's Ford inverse-fibre propagation lemma takes a given totient d with its full inverse fibre and shows that many v = dφ(b) inherit a fibre of the same size, which presupposes d and says nothing about whether a singleton fibre exists; (iii) the 'exactly one' in collisions.tex concerns tuples in the prefix map, not preimages of values under φ.
